title: Hyperelliptic period parity with PARI
objective: Fuse exact completed-model validation, qqbar topology, independent Arb/Acb refinements, Riemann and conjugation validation, real-lattice assembly, and bounded Abel--Jacobi point batches behind mature FLINT operations while retaining ordinary-source witnesses and measuring exact genus-2/3 PARI and Magma contracts

exceptions: The canonical compiler cannot yet lower variable-precision qqbar/Arb/Acb matrices or FLINT exact integer kernel/SNF resources. The bounded mature-FLINT operation mirrors the ordinary Python topology, panel quadrature, Riemann, conjugation, and lattice formulas; has no host callbacks after entry; publishes only after two arbitrary-precision refinements; and retains a lazily materialized ordinary-source witness plus exact differential and PARI oracles. These representations should become declared compiler resources when supported.

handoff.summary: Commits 4b0e069b and c5ac3082 deliver the fused complete Arb/Acb period operation and exact bench-1 PARI receipt: resident 64-bit g2/g3 ratios are 1.7273x and 1.46594x. Commit 92dae550 adds public bounded Abel--Jacobi batches: exact point validation, one qqbar root isolation and ray plan per batch, three increasing Arb/Acb refinement witnesses, ordinary-source replay, and a correct scalar capability fallback. The exact bench-1 Magma receipt records a 151.952 ms public 12-point Sage.js median versus 1420 ms for twelve separate Magma ToAnalyticJacobian calls sharing one prepared AnalyticJacobian, a 9.345x batch win.
risks: Integration must classify the new napi:@sagemath/sagejs-flint:hyperellipticAbelJacobiBatchArb export and regenerate native inventories before architecture:check and the full native suite can be final.

Magma and Sage.js choose different homology bases, so the receipt retains both numeric outputs but uses exact point equations, conjugate-pair cancellation, and Sage.js ordinary-source replay instead of asserting coordinate equality across bases.

The Abel batch reaches 38 measured stability bits for this 64-bit request while retaining 64-bit Arb arithmetic accuracy and independent 96/128/160-bit refinements; the already-integrated period path still preserves its separate greater-than-44-bit two-refinement acceptance evidence.
Platforms without the FLINT host capability remain mathematically correct through the ordinary scalar fallback but do not receive the batch performance improvement.
next_steps: Classify hyperellipticAbelJacobiBatchArb as a retained hyperelliptic external-library host adapter and regenerate the export inventory.
Rebuild the FLINT addon after integration, rerun the focused period/Abel test, architecture:check, and test:native against the rebuilt addon.

Record non-acceptance cross-architecture performance receipts on bench-arm and m1 when their FLINT addon builds are available; keep Windows on the tested capability fallback until the native dependency stack is supported there.
